hints: Focus on how many C=C bonds can react, the words an excess of dry HBr tell you every alkene will undergo addition.
Recall Markovnikov's rule for HBr, H adds to the carbon with more H atoms so that the more stable tertiary carbocation forms and Br ends up on the more substituted carbon.
Apply that rule separately to the trisubstituted ring C=C and to the terminal exocyclic C=CH2, both should give a tertiary C-Br with a methyl group on the same carbon.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two alkenes**

Look closely at the starting material. It is a diene with two different C=C bonds.

Top: a trisubstituted ring alkene, $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=CH}$, bottom: an exocyclic terminal alkene, $\text{C=CH}_2$.

**Recall electrophilic addition of HBr**

Dry HBr adds across C=C by Markovnikov addition.

$$\text{C=C + HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH-CBr}$$

**Apply Markovnikov to each bond**

H goes to the carbon that already has more H, Br goes to the more alkyl substituted carbon via the most stable carbocation.

Top bond: H to $\text{CH}$, Br to $\text{C-CH}_3$ gives $\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)}$. Bottom bond: H to $\text{CH}_2$ gives $\text{CH}_3$, Br to ring C gives $\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)}.$

**Build product Z**

Both additions give a tertiary bromide on the same carbon as a methyl group.

That is 1,4-dibromo-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane, with Br at the top tertiary position and Br at the bottom tertiary position.

options.A: This has Br on the carbon next to the top methyl group, a secondary bromide. That is anti-Markovnikov for the ring alkene. The top carbocation would be secondary instead of the more stable tertiary, so this is not the major product.
options.B: This shows Br and CH3 on the same carbon at the top and Br and CH3 on the same carbon at the bottom. Both are tertiary bromides formed by Markovnikov addition to the two C=C bonds, giving the most stable carbocation intermediates. This is the major product Z.
options.C: This shows a $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ group at the bottom, a primary bromide. That is anti-Markovnikov addition to the $\text{C=CH}_2$ bond, via a less stable primary carbocation. It also puts Br next to the top methyl, so both additions are the wrong way round.
options.D: The top is correct Markovnikov tertiary bromide, but the bottom is $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$, a primary bromide. Students choosing this correctly do the ring alkene but forget Markovnikov for the terminal alkene, where H must add to $\text{CH}_2$ to make $\text{CH}_3$.
